clue.text: The Goldwood Trial

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold
deal is pine or fir timber sawn into planks

explanation.surface: It reads like the title of a court case or a film: The Goldwood Trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goldwood' looks like a surname or place name, but it is two words run together. Gold comes from heraldry, and the wood is the plain pine timber used in carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial in the sense of a severe test or painful experience is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Trade union in retreat overturned custom

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
in a down clue, overturned means the word for retreat is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den, a place to retreat to

explanation.surface: A union pulls back and abandons a long-held workplace practice.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'overturned' turns the den word upside down, giving RIAL, and 'in' sets the union inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is an established practice repeated by habit, which is what a ritual is.

clue.text: Infuriated snake in river and goddess in road

indicators.note: the snake goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: the goddess's name sits inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Someone driven mad by a snake in a river and a goddess blocking the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in Devon; Ate is the Greek goddess of folly. EX-ASP-E then R-ATE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be infuriated is to be extremely annoyed, a close synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Member on stage

definitions.meaning: a limb of the body, such as one used for walking
a section of a journey or race, as in the first part of a relay

explanation.surface: An actor or member of a company appearing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a bodily member, and one section of a journey is called by the same word.

clue.text: Load imported by Parisian is cooked snail

indicators.note: the load is brought into the French word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: est is French for 'is'
a cargo is a load carried by a ship or plane

explanation.surface: A shipment brought in by a Parisian turns out to be a plate of cooked snails.
explanation.definitionFit: The French culinary term for an edible snail prepared as food, typically with garlic butter.

clue.text: Old chairs PM chucked out before prime-time broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letters P and M are thrown out of the words prime-time

parts.note: the letters P and M as written

explanation.surface: Retired professors watch as the Prime Minister is ejected before a peak-hour TV slot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucked out' takes P and M from PRIMETIME, leaving RIETIME, which 'broadcast' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairs here are professorships or professors; retired professors keeping their title are emeriti.

clue.text: Last character in churches gives nationality

indicators.note: the last letter goes inside the church abbreviations

parts.note: CE (Church of England) and CH are both abbreviations for church, so two churches give CE and CH
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A final character found in churches reveals someone's nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last character' means the last letter of the alphabet, not the last letter of a word. 'in' puts Z inside CE+CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Czech Republic has this nationality.

clue.text: Undeviating routine somewhat brutal

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the word brutal is taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A rigid, monotonous routine that is rather harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck in a groove means following the same dull routine without change.

clue.text: Bloomer unknown to occur in old language

indicators.note: the unknown is placed so as to appear inside the old language letters

parts.note: a tongue is a language
X is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A mistake, by someone unknown, made in an ancient language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; here it means a flowering plant. 'to occur in' puts X between O and TONGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and oxtongue is a yellow-flowered weed of the daisy family.

clue.text: Suppress line in novel

indicators.note: the line letter goes inside the word for novel

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new and unusual, so strange

explanation.surface: An editor cutting a line from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the adjective meaning unfamiliar.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress a laugh or a scream is to choke it back, which is the figurative sense here.

clue.text: Denied first time in having valid will for assets

indicators.note: the leading time letter is refused, taken off the front of the legal term

parts.note: a person who dies testate has left a valid will

explanation.surface: Someone refused their first chance to make a valid will for their property.
explanation.walkthrough: TESTATE is a legal word for having made a valid will; 'Denied first' strips its opening T.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's assets, all the property they own, make up their estate.

clue.text: Perverse Pierre drops guts in prison division

indicators.note: those outer letters go inside the prison division

parts.note: a ward is a section of a prison or hospital

indicators.note: Pierre loses its insides, so only its outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A twisted Frenchman disembowelling someone in a prison wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops guts' leaves P and E from Pierre, which 'in' puts inside WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something warped has been bent out of shape, used of a twisted, perverse mind.

clue.text: Scenery firm in Derby's not near

indicators.note: the firm goes inside what is left
not says the word for near is left out of the city name

parts.note: Derby, the English city, with the 's as a possessive
by means near, as in 'stand by me'
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A firm of scenery-makers in Derby that is not nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not near' looks like a description of distance; it says to drop the word meaning near from the city's name, leaving DER, and 'in' puts the firm inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage scenery is often called by this French-derived word for the setting or furnishings.

clue.text: Cruel and stupid to constrict busy sound

indicators.note: the word for stupid squeezes round the sound, holding it inside

parts.note: inane means silly or stupid
a hum is the sound of busy activity, as in a hive

explanation.surface: A harsh and foolish attempt to stifle a busy noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane treatment is treatment lacking compassion, that is, cruel.

clue.text: Release football team getting goal

parts.note: Man U is short for Manchester United, the English football club
a mission is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A football side signing a player who scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' looks like a score in football; here it means aim. MAN U is Manchester United, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal term for releasing someone from slavery.

clue.text: Old leg-breaker buried each in ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are pounded into a new order

explanation.surface: A former bone-breaking thug buried each victim in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Richie Benaud was an Australian cricket captain and leg-spin bowler, later a famous TV commentator. A leg-break is a ball spun from the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-breaker is a cricket bowler of leg-spin, and this Australian was one of the best, now deceased.

clue.text: Develop physique

definitions.meaning: to construct or put up, make grow
a person's bodily frame or shape

explanation.surface: Bodybuilding advice: develop your physique.
explanation.definitionFit: To construct something is to develop it, and a person's bodily frame is also called this word.

clue.text: Brought about conscious state

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for brought is read backwards

parts.note: led means brought, guided along
aware means conscious

explanation.surface: Something brought about a state of consciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought about' looks like one phrase meaning caused; 'about' is the reversal signal on LED, giving DEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is a US state, the first to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: Doctrine is set in Roman reworking

indicators.note: reworking means redoing, so these letters are refashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctrine set down in a Roman revision of the text.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Christian doctrine named after Nestorius, a 5th-century patriarch condemned as a heretic.

clue.text: One more heart on for transplant?

indicators.note: transplanting moves things to new positions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient waiting for yet another heart transplant.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for one more of something is asking for an additional one, which is what the word means.

clue.text: Exchange old German coin and French

parts.note: the mark was Germany's currency before the euro
the word 'and' in French is et

explanation.surface: Swapping old German money and French currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and French' is the French word for 'and', not a separate item.
explanation.definitionFit: A market, like a stock exchange, is a place where goods are traded.

clue.text: One's pride displayed on beach in coastal location

indicators.note: the letters for one's pride are placed after the beach, following on from it

parts.note: sand is what covers a beach
one is I, the Roman numeral, with the 's leading to pride
ego means self-esteem or pride

explanation.surface: Someone showing off their vanity on the beach at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: This Californian city is on the Pacific coast near the Mexican border.

clue.text: Chap first in every test has achieved notoriety

indicators.note: first in says to take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A man who came first in every exam has become famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first in every test' looks like the boast; 'first in' takes the first letter of each of the five words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chap is a man, and this is a man's name, so a crossword-only example of one.

clue.text: Miserable face sergeant major wears

indicators.note: the face holds the abbreviation as if wearing it, with it inside

parts.note: dial is slang for face

explanation.surface: A sergeant major with a gloomy expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and miserable both describe gloomy, depressing weather or moods.

clue.text: Scot's road in mess

definitions.note: a Scot is, with 's as 'is' linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: the road goes inside the word for mess

parts.note: a hash is a mess, as in 'make a hash of it'
M1 is the main motorway from London to the north of England, written here as MI

explanation.surface: A Scottish road that is in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; the 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a typical Scottish man's first name, the Gaelic form of James.

clue.text: Dicky's hostile

definitions.meaning: dicky is British slang for unwell or weak, as in a dicky heart; 's is 'is'
unfriendly, as in bad will or feeling

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky is unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name; it is British slang for unwell or shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick and unfriendly are both senses of the word, as in feeling poorly and bearing ill will.

clue.text: Capital's decline in endless spiral

definitions.note: a capital is, with the 's as 'is' linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: the decline goes inside the shortened spiral
endless says the last letter of the spiral word is cut off

parts.note: a helix is a spiral shape
to sink is to decline

explanation.surface: A financial crash: capital's value dropping in an endless downward spiral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter from the spiral word, leaving HELI, and 'in' puts the decline inside it. The surface sounds financial; the capital is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Good riddance to happy and stable employee

indicators.note: good riddance says the good letter is got rid of from the word for happy

parts.note: glad means happy

explanation.surface: Good riddance, says someone happy, to a dependable worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like steady; it is a place for horses. 'Good riddance' is split: G is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable lad is a young groom who looks after racehorses.

clue.text: German in ship chasing British monarch

indicators.note: the ship follows behind the British monarch, coming after it

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A German on board a ship racing after the British queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Berlin, Germany's capital, is a German of that city.

clue.text: Female keeping back beat to contribute

indicators.note: the female holds the reversed letters inside her

parts.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit

indicators.note: back means the word for beat is read in reverse

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: A woman holding back from beating someone in order to give something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads the word for beat in reverse, giving NAT, and 'keeping' has the female deer hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: To contribute to charity is to give money to it, a straight synonym.
